selected_evidence.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations
selected_evidence.summary: The installed configuration contains daily, rotate 7, and compress; logrotate parses it as one-day rotation with seven rotations.

selected_evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
selected_evidence.summary: A held-open writer emitted a pre-rotation marker, logrotate copied/truncated and compressed the file, then the same writer emitted a post-rotation marker into the active log. Both markers were verified in their expected files.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
selected_evidence.summary: Before and after work, node1 remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64; the existing RHEL logrotate 3.18.0 package was used.

Healthy baseline boot ID c2f29441-0515-4717-99f7-a7647824278d was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, and the recovered node reported changed boot ID 908613c4-98a9-4077-9d49-d2d00eefd2f2. Post-restart state was running with the logrotate timer enabled/active, policy and rotated data intact, and zero failed units.

commands.command:
set -eu
pre_marker="rotation_pre_$(date +%s)"
post_marker="rotation_post_$(date +%s)"
export pre_marker post_marker
bash -c 'exec 3>>/var/log/inventory/app.log; printf "%s\n" "$pre_marker" >&3; sleep 3; printf "%s\n" "$post_marker" >&3; exec 3>&-' &
writer_pid=$!
i=0
while ! grep -F "$pre_marker" /var/log/inventory/app.log >/dev/null 2>&1; do i=$((i+1)); [ "$i" -lt 20 ] || exit 1; sleep 1; done
printf 'PRE_ROTATION_WRITER_PID=%s MARKER=%s\n' "$writer_pid" "$pre_marker"
logrotate -v -f -s /tmp/inventory-logrotate-test.status /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app
wait "$writer_pid"
printf 'ROTATED_FILES\n'; ls -l /var/log/inventory/app.log*
printf 'ROTATED_HAS_PRE='; zgrep -F "$pre_marker" /var/log/inventory/app.log.1.gz
printf 'ACTIVE_HAS_POST='; grep -F "$post_marker" /var/log/inventory/app.log
printf 'ACTIVE_INODE='; stat -c '%i size=%s mode=%a owner=%U:%G' /var/log/inventory/app
